children: , an artificial intelligence (AI) company focused on medical diagnostics for faster and more accurate treatment decisions in wound care, today reflected on its successful participation at the Southern Regional Burn Conference (SRBC), held September 10-12, 2026 in Williamsburg, Virginia.

The Company’s DeepView® System for Burn Indication was on display for attending burn care clinicians and was the subject of KOL presentations that support the use of AI and multispectral imaging in the assessment of burn wounds:
Artificial Intelligence Evaluation of Multispectral Imaging Improves Physician Accuracy in Detecting Non-Healing Burn Wounds
James Hwang, MD, UAB, Birmingham, AL
Repeatability and Reproducibility of Artificial Intelligence Analysis of Burn Wound Multispectral Imaging
Jeffrey Carter, MD, FACS,FABA, Burn and Trauma at UMCNO, New Orleans, LA

“We were pleased to engage with burn care clinicians and thought leaders at the SRBC and to showcase the DeepView System’s potential to support faster, more informed treatment decisions,” said Vincent S. Capone, Chief Executive Officer. “Following the FDA’s De Novo Classification of the DeepView System earlier this year, we remain focused on advancing adoption of our technology and supporting clinicians with immediate, objective data that can help guide patient care.”

“As burn surgeons, we are constantly making treatment decisions to optimize outcomes for our patients,” said Dr. James Hwang, Director, UAB Burn Center, Chief, Burn Service. “The significant improvement in diagnostic evaluation, with AI assistance, is encouraging and suggests that DeepView could provide valuable additional insight when making these important treatment determinations.”

Spectral AI's DeepView System is a non-invasive, predictive medical device that combines multispectral imaging with a proprietary AI algorithm to assess the healing potential of areas within burn wounds. It was granted De Novo Classification by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (“FDA”) in May 2026 and received its initial UKCA (UK Conformity Assessed) authorization in the United Kingdom in February 2024. The DeepView System provides physicians with an immediate, data-driven assessment of whether areas within burn wounds are unlikely to heal within 21 days and may require significant medical intervention, enabling earlier and more informed treatment decisions. The image acquisition takes 0.2 seconds, and all image processing and AI model classification takes approximately 20 to 25 seconds. The DeepView System is trained and tested against a proprietary and clinically validated database of over 340 billion pixels of burn wound image data.

The MRBC serves as a central gathering point for the burn care community across the Midwest and Eastern Great Lakes regions. It supports the professionals who care for burn patients at every stage by providing practical education, sharing best practices, and strengthening the connections that support coordinated, team-based care.

The NRBC brings together a multidisciplinary community of burn-care professionals, including physicians, nurses, physician assistants, nurse practitioners, physical therapists, occupational therapists, residents, fellows, social workers, case managers, psychologists, nutritionists, burn technicians, students, pharmacists, firefighters, education outreach personnel and other members of the burn care team.​
The NRBC will feature the following KOL presentation:
Artificial Intelligence Evaluation of Multispectral Imaging Improves Physician Accuracy in Detecting Non-Healing Burn Wounds
Alisa Savetamal, MD, FACS, FABA, Connecticut Burn Center, Bridgeport, CT

Spectral AI, Inc. is a Dallas-based predictive AI company focused on medical diagnostics for faster and more accurate treatment decisions in wound care, with initial applications involving patients with burns. The Company is working to revolutionize the management of wound care by “Seeing the Unknown®” with its DeepView System. The DeepView System is a predictive diagnostic device that offers physicians an objective and immediate assessment of a wound’s healing potential prior to treatment or other medical intervention. With algorithm-driven results and a goal to exceed the current standard of care, the DeepView System provides fast and accurate treatment insights to improve patient outcomes and reduce healthcare costs.
